note: The sandbox base. pos is [x, z] in metres from the patch centre (+X east, -Z north), yaw degrees clockwise from north. Heights come from the terrain. Laid out as a real surface outpost (design/research/layout.md): HAB 1, the greenhouse and the storm shelter with their doors on one yard south of the airlock, the gas bottles at the airlock, the power yard (battery bank) east between the sun-tracking wing field and the users, the dish north in open sky, the rover in a charging bay by the power yard, and the two things NASA keeps 1 km off (the reactor, the lander) in opposite corners of the play area (play_half), about 190 m out. Curiosity and Mont Mercou stand at their own field sites (`sites`), reached by rover: they are really 14.3 km and 8.8 km away.

items._note: at its sol 5070 spot on Mount Sharp, the curiosity field site's middle (data/world.json sites), heading back south on its route (team blog, sols 5063 to 5069). Look and photograph only: it is working, driven from Earth
at the mercou field site, beside the site's middle, where Curiosity stood on sols 3049 to 3079 (data/world.json sites)

the ride home on its own lander (forge/building_mav.py). Real: landers about 1 km apart (SAC21, NTRS 20210026448), here the south-west corner of the play area, 191 m out and 270 m from the crew lander, as the reactor and the lander are (design/research/layout.md); the fuel gauge and hatch face the base
the one disposal spot, next to the crew lander (SAC21: 'next to the lander as its permanent disposal location'), its label toward the rover track's end
south of the yard in open ground, clear of the rover track; its panel faces north, the sun's side at Gale
beside the dish, west of it, off the dish's cable

sites._note: field sites the crew visits by rover with a time skip (cine trip_to): each a separate walkable patch of real HiRISE ground (tools/site_terrain.py from a 1 m DTM window, terrain.gd add_site()), placed far from the base in world space, past the camera's 8 km far plane and the fog, so neither is ever seen from the other (15 km out: the base's backdrop reaches 6.2 km, a ring 3.6 km). The real distance lives in km, bearing and up_m (from the base; research/junior-astronaut/mission-collisions.md, our great-circle maths on NASA's MSL waypoint file), never in world metres. half: m from a site's centre that anything that moves may go (world.bound(margin, at)); its patch is 200 m across. ring: m the site's own slope carries on past its edge into the fog, with no collision. Landmarks: site_<id> where the hero looks from, site_<id>_rover where the rover arrives

cables._note: power cables laid on the ground (world.gd _lay_cables): polylines of [x, z], draped on height_at() every step m, width and height in metres, in a DESIGN.md role; rocks keep off them as off paths. Each line runs between two devices, `ends` in the same order: 'item:node' names the empty in the device's model where it plugs in (port_1 when left out), and the line's first and last points move onto it, so the cable ends inside the gland box on the ground that the model carries, under a conduit up into the device (forge/base_kit.py port(); a cable stopping beside its device read as unplugged, 13 Nov playtest). Power runs source to yard to user: the reactor and the wings into the battery bank (battery..battery3, the power yard east of HAB 1; each cabinet has port_n and port_s on its north and south ends), and out of it to each user (the greenhouse and the yard light through HAB 1). Layout and its sources: design/research/layout.md. In order: the reactor's 3 kVac line (real: 1 km, NTRS 20250000841; our ground is real and swept to 150 m, so it comes from the north-east corner of that, 191 m out) into battery3; the wing field's header from battery3 to wing 1's junction box, then box to box along the rows' north ends (each box has port_w and port_e, the field's combiner chain; wing 6's port_e stays capped); HAB 1 (its east feed box, port_e2); HAB 1 on to the greenhouse round the north side, clear of both doors; the dish; the north work light; the rover's charging post in its bay (SAC21: the crew 'connect the PR to the surface power grid to recharge batteries'; the post's own lead to the rover is `charger`); the yard light, off HAB 1's port_e1. No line crosses a path, the lander track or a doorway (tests/world_test.gd), so no cover ramp is needed. Size and routes are ours

charger._note: the rover's charging post in its bay (world.gd _charger, forge/prop_charger.py): with the rover parked and still for still_s seconds and its port_charge within reach_m of the post's lead_out, the plug sits in the rover's socket and the post's light glows; once the rover moves drift_m the plug is back in the post's holster. The lead is lead_m long and width thick, in a DESIGN.md role. Motion and light only. Lengths are ours (a car charger's lead is 5 to 7.5 m; a short one keeps it in the bay)

flags._note: the team's flag on the hulls, as crews mark a vehicle (world.gd _flags): the flag of Sri Lanka, the real file from Wikimedia Commons, public domain, never redrawn or recoloured (ASSETS.md), in its own 1:2 proportions. Each row is a flat, lit quad on the `part` of `item` that moves (the rover's sprung `body`, the rocket's `ascent` stage that cine.gd launch() flies), in that part's own space: `pos` a point on the hull's surface, `out` the way the hull faces there, `width` in m (the height is half of it); `off`: m it stands off the hull so the two faces never flicker. The picture reads the same on both sides of the rover, the lion toward the hoist, never mirrored. Rover: each side of the cabin, at the left of CLAMOR as seen from outside (so toward the rear on +X and toward the window pillar on -X), its middle on the letters' middle line, one and a half letters tall, half its height clear of the word; flag and word together are as wide as ROVER 1 under them, and the block is centred in the flat panel between the window pillar and the rear corner, over the locker (forge/vehicle_rover.py places the lettering: move both together). Rocket: stage 1's back (the side of the CLAMOR lettering, which the launch camera films), under the name, between the lower and middle bands; flat on a 2.25 m drum, so its ends stand 6 cm proud: a wider one needs a bent quad. Places and sizes are art direction (0.41 m and 1 m wide beside the 1.8 m hero)

bound._note: where anything that moves may go: |x| and |z| up to half (m from the patch centre). The ground is real only on the 400 m patch (data/terrain.json, half 200): past it the backdrop is drawn with no collision, and height_at() reads the patch edge. 190 keeps a body's reach inside it: the rover's centre stays reach (m, its rear hatch) further in, and the cameras behind (5 m on foot, 9 m driving) stay over the patch. Near the line the hero and the rover slow at their own braking (reality.json hero.stop, rover.brake) and stop on it. The safety net (sandbox.gd): a body found more than below (m) under the ground, or past the line, goes back on top at the nearest spot inside, behind a short fade (fade_s) when that is further than fade_over (m). Art direction

kinds._note: how an item collides; anything not named here is a static (layer 2, or 3 when narrower than the hero)

sink._note: how far each prefab sits in the dust: a reality.json row id per prefab, else default (skills/shadows-and-grounding, Sink). support: metres above an item's lowest drawn point that still count as resting on the ground (feet, skids, bevelled bottom edges). level: prefabs crews build level (floors, foundations, tracking mounts); everything else tilts to the ground under it, as a lander's legs or a bag do. Vehicles only touch: their drivers set them on their wheels, sunk by their own row here (rover). Rocks: reality.json rock.embed

graded._note: prefabs whose footprint (standin size) is graded level before the ground is built (world/terrain.gd _grade()), as crews prepare a site before they lay a slab on it: NASA's ASPECT project 'will develop tools and methods to clear, level, and compact the lunar surface' (https://www.nasa.gov/?p=96252, design/research/pages/pad-grading/). Without it a 0.15 m pad on a slope was buried at its uphill side and the ground came up through it; the greenhouse's and the shelter's floors showed the ground through them the same way (13 Nov playtest), and HAB 1's doorway (14 Nov: deck 2 mm over the ground). A standin spans the model's whole footprint about its origin where it matters (the greenhouse's vestibule reaches 4.71 m out; HAB 1's porch, 4.23 m, lies within 3 cm of level as it is), and neighbours' grades stay apart on the 2 m grid: a later one overwrites an earlier one where they meet (world_test checks every graded footprint is level, 14 Nov)

_swept_range_m: metres from the camera to a ground cell's centre (the patch centre for the base) beyond which its swept surfaces (floors, HAB 1's fit-out: DESIGN.md weathering.clean) are not drawn: seen only through doorways, they cost a draw call each from anywhere (world.gd _merge). Art direction

blink._note: status lights that flash on their own (world/machines.gd): nodes named by `nodes` keep their own mesh and a copy of the light role. hz and duty: an obstruction beacon flashes 20 to 40 times a minute (FAA L-864 red 20 to 40, L-865 white 40, https://www.faa.gov/documentLibrary/media/Advisory_Circular/150-5345-43GH.pdf, from a search summary); WCAG 2.3.1 allows at most 3 flashes in any second. off: the share of the light left when it is dark

machines._note: the base working on its own (world/machines.gd). tracker: solar panels start facing the sun and turn to it about their tube at slew_deg_s (after a sky switch or a tilt by hand) within limit_deg (30 keeps a panel's low edge at the 0.82 m of its 30 degree rest, above a walker's knees), re-aiming when the sun is step_deg off, lying flat (stow) where weather says stow (night, storm), and holding still for pause_s after anyone else moves one (the tilt interaction). dish: nods nod_deg either side of its rest every period_s at slew_deg_s. near_m: panels and dish hold still while the hero is this close (a machine stops when people come near). All art direction; servo: the sound each move starts with, played only within hear_m (Mars sound 'falters at just 26 feet (8 meters)', NASA/JPL 2022)

tracker._rows: per prefab: gcr, the ground coverage ratio of its rows (panel chord over row pitch), with which the rows backtrack toward flat when the sun is low enough for a row to shade the next (Anderson and Mikofski 2020, NREL/TP-5K00-76626; pvlib tracking.singleaxis, whose example is 2 m modules 6 m apart, gcr 1/3; design/research/pages/tracker/). solar_wing: 2.5 m wings 7.5 m apart, the six rows running north and south as single-axis trackers usually do (Sandia PVPMC), turning to limit_deg 45, 'common' for trackers (Sandia PVPMC); its low edge then stands 0.57 m up, and the field has no walkway under it

telltale._note: Phoenix's Telltale (2008): a light Kapton tube on Kevlar fibres from a gallows on the met mast, its tilt read off camera images. tilt: [wind m/s, tilt rad] at 8 mbar, read off Fig. 25 of the Telltale calibration report (Gunnlaugsson et al., https://pds.nasa.gov/data/pds4/1000/tt_bundle_1000/document/TELLTALECALRPT.PDF; design/research/pages/alive/telltale.md): thin air barely moves it, about 1 degree at 4 m/s. flutter: the share of the tilt it trembles by (the report reads turbulence from the image blur), flutter_hz how fast; art direction

grounding._note: the ground's answer under everything that rests on it (world.rest(), terrain.gdshader): a soft darkening where the sky is blocked (AO scales the ambient light only, skills/shadows-and-grounding section 4) plus a little in the albedo, and a faint rim of dust pushed up around the edge (a normal tilt). radius: m a foot's shadow reaches past it; ao, albedo: how much at the foot; pile: the rim's strength; px: the map's pixels over play_half; set_down_speed (m/s) and set_down_strength: the grit a bag throws when it is put down (world.puff). Art direction

paths._note: walkways kept clear of rocks: polylines of [x, z], width in metres. From the airlock yard: south, to the rover's hatch, to the power yard, to the greenhouse door, past the storm shelter's door to build pad 1; the dish path north; the rover's track from its bay to the lander, 191 m north-west (design/research/layout.md)

scatter._note: rocks over the patch: none on items, pads or paths, densest just outside the base clearing. Sizes in metres; rocks in big_size are solid, pebbles are not

wind._note: toward_deg: where the wind blows to, degrees clockwise from north (a design choice: no measured Gale direction found). Speeds per sky state in weather: Ingenuity's dust drifted downwind at 4 to 6 m/s (research/godot-build/movement-and-look.md section 4)
wind._gust: gust(): one slow swell every wind listener reads (dust streaks, the wind sound, the telltale; skills/living-atmosphere section 2). gust_hz: the noise's frequency, so a swell takes tens of seconds; share: how far a gust takes the sky state's speed above or below it. Both art direction: no measured Gale gust timing in our sources

weather._note: dust effects per sky state, keyed by the DESIGN.<state>.md name. streaks: share of the wind streaks shown; devil: the far dust devil (summer afternoons, NASA 2017); front: the storm's close dust clouds; stow: the solar trackers lie flat (no sun at night; trackers stow flat in high wind)

contact._note: footstep and wheel dust (skills/ground-contact-fx, design/research/dust.md). Grit: grains over ~70 um launched at 30 to 60 deg (Kok 2012), each gone when it lands, T = 2 v sin(theta) / g with g from reality.json; a wheel throws them backward and low (fenders, NASM 2015). Haze: dust under ~20 um in the bottom few cm, spreading then drifting downwind and gone in 2 to 3 s (Lemmon 2022). min_speed (nothing thrown standing still), counts, sizes (grit_size: a few pixels at the 4.2 m play camera, ground-contact-fx section 3), alpha and the speed spread are art direction. foot_kick: the share of the walking speed a boot's push-off scuffs grit backward at (the boot is nearly still at contact; ground-contact-fx section 2), art direction. wheel_grit, wheel_grit_size, wheel_haze: a rolling wheel's steady stream (dust.stream()): grains alive at once, their size (a few pixels at the 9 m driving camera, ground-contact-fx section 3) haze quads alive at once, their peak alpha and size (a 3 t rover lifts more fine dust than a boot, and grit the ground's colour vanishes against the ground); art direction

devil._note: the dust devil wanders round the base centre this far out, in and out by the share `wander`, at this speed in m/s; day only (weather), the summer afternoons NASA saw them at Gale (sol 1597). All design choices (no measured Gale speed in our sources): slow enough to watch, outside the lander and Curiosity, near enough to see from the base (at 160 m it did not show)
devil._devils: devils: [radius m, start angle rad, size], each on its own circle round the centre, every other one the other way, at the same ground speed (world/dust.gd). Four spread round the crater (a playtester asked for more, 14 Nov). More than Gale shows at once: its whirlwinds peak 11:00 to 13:00, about one a sol in the pressure record, and Curiosity imaged 214 unique dust devils in the foothills over sols 1545 to 1660, most lifting little dust (research/junior-astronaut/factcheck.md rows 175, 176); four in view at once is art direction. Radii from 125 m (tests/devil_test.gd: never within 80 m of a base building, Ravindu 14 Nov: devils are scenery and never enter the base) to 160 m (it barely shows)

probe._note: one reflection probe over the base: centre [x, z], size [x, y, z]. The sandbox redraws every probe from this centre looking at HAB 1 after a sky switch (HouseStyle.warm(), sandbox.gd _probe_view()), and a probe is drawn only once a camera sees it: the centre sits 10 m out from HAB 1 so the room probes are in view (the whole base turned to face the sunrise, 14 Nov, tools/rotate_base.py). rooms: an item's own probe, centre `at` and `size` in its space (HAB 1: the room between the deck at 0.40 m and the ceiling at 2.72 m; the greenhouse: the dome, `interior` false so its glass shows the sky). light: the room's own light (world.gd restyle(), DESIGN.md lighting.room), at `at` in the item's space with its `range` in m and `color` a DESIGN.md colour name (default lighting.room.color), `share` of lighting.room.intensity (default 1; the grow light at full strength turned the greenhouse floor magenta by day): HAB 1's and the shelter's in the middle of the room, between floor and ceiling (14 Nov playtest: hung 10 to 17 cm under the ceiling, it lit a hot spot round the panels and left the walls and floor dim at night), the greenhouse's the grow light at the rack tops in the `grow` magenta. The storm shelter: the room between its floor at 0.06 m and its ceiling at 2.5 m. It stands west of this centre, out of the warm-up camera's view, so its probe is drawn the first time the play camera sees it

pip._note: PIP's wandering (sandbox/pip.gd): ambient life, no game state. Speed, acceleration and turn: reality.json pip.*. Everything here is art direction. stops: where it parks [x, z] and what it looks at [x, z, height above the ground], weight how often it picks one; via: open ground it may drive through, so the route graph (every straight, clear line between stops and via points, `clearance` m clear either side) gets round the buildings ([-10.5, 7.0], between the greenhouse door and the storm shelter's west side: once the shelter grew, a PIP nudged against its corner found no short line home and went round by the lander, 14 Nov sols_test); via_m: how near a via point counts as passed;  (the lander is a long trip), divided by near_m plus the distance so near stops come up more; never one of the last two. notice_m: the hero this close gets a look, a beep and two flashes (flash_hz under the 3 a second limit), at most every hello_cool_s. A hero standing still (below still_speed m/s for still_s) within greet_m gets a visit: PIP parks greet_stand_m away, looks up with its head tilted, wiggles, for greet_s, then not again for greet_cool_s. yield_m, yield_deg: a hero this close inside this cone ahead stops it for wait_s, then it drives round for patience_s. feeler_m: how far ahead it checks, every feel_s; stuck_s without getting 0.3 m closer and it backs out and plans again (an order: again and again; wandering, the second time it goes elsewhere); wedge_s neither moving nor turning (boxed in between bags) and it backs out reverse_m along its trail (a point every trail_m) before planning again. Bags and the rover are planned round, the hero is left to the feelers. door_clear_m round every door and rooms (prefabs, grown by room_margin) it never drives into. flee_m: a moving rover this close sends it aside. Head: yaw and pitch limits, turn rate, tilt; blinks every blink_s, double_blink share; status bar glows at glow_hz. track_every, track_width: m between wheel prints (a print is 0.24 m long, world/terrain.gd, so under that they join into a band) and their width (the wheel is 8 cm wide, forge/vehicle_pip.py); track_depth: the prints' depth and darkness (terrain.mark strength; the rover's are tuning.json rover.track_depth, 0.5 at a crawl to 1 at speed, the hero's boots 1). Art direction from the physics: sinkage grows with the pressure under the wheel (Bekker), and a small robot's light load on narrow wheels barely marks the dust where a crewed rover's 0.99 m wheels leave a rut (Curiosity's 0.5 m wheels sank under 1 cm on Gale's plains, reality.json ground.sink.soft), so a faint scuff: a fifth of the rover's crawl; shade: contact shadow radius and strength

views._note: eye-height capture views inside rooms (sandbox.gd set_view): [item id, from, at], both in the item's own space (its front, the door, toward -Z; y over the model's lowest point), so they follow the item if it moves. The eye is 1.6 m over the floor (HAB 1's deck at 0.40 m, the greenhouse floor at 0.20 m). n, e, s, w: the compass way the view looks (HAB 1 stands at yaw 180, so its own +Z is north). hab_eye_bed and hab_eye_wc look straight at the berths and into the toilet. gh_eye_a looks in from the vestibule down the aisle, gh_eye_b back from the far end. The storm shelter's floor is at 0.06 m: sh_eye_in looks from inside its door at the bunks, sh_eye_left at the comms screen and radiation sign, sh_eye_rack at the water and food rack, sh_eye_door back at the door
views._w: lane W's capture views of its items (13 Nov): each from in front of the item; sky_earth from the yard north of HAB 1 up into the west-south-west evening sky, where Earth and Venus stand after sunset (capture it at an evening hour, sky_earth@19.6)

rooms._note: the buildings with an inside (player.gd _room: the rules, the sound, the lights; follow_cam.gd keeps the third-person lens in the plan, skills/third-person-camera Rooms): each item id's floor plan in its own space, circles [x, z, r] and rects [x0, z0, x1, z1], measured from the models (12 Nov). hab1: building_habitat.glb floor x and z +-2.40, the door's inner face at z -2.16. greenhouse: building_greenhouse.glb floor +-3.28 (the dome), and the vestibule x +-1.0 from the door's inner face at z -4.46 to the dome. shelter (13 Nov): building_storm_shelter.glb, the bags' inside faces at x +-2.0, the back at z 1.75, the door frame's inner face at z -1.75 (14 Nov, 4.0 x 3.5 m: it was 2.6 x 2.5). The doorway band is the hero's own radius either side of these lines

plants._note: lettuce in the greenhouse grow-bed slots (slot_N nodes of its model), one growth stage per slot; stage 4 is a harvest-size head (reality.json lettuce.width). A number is red romaine 'Outredgeous' (Veggie VEG-01), "green_N" stage N of a green lettuce ('Waldmann's Green', VEG-03): the lower tier at hand height (slots 1-4, 9-12) is green, like the leaf the harvest spots pick. A prefab id instead of a stage goes in at its own size: HAB 1's Veggie unit on the galley counter

uses._note: use spots (design/plans/next-lanes.md section 0; sandbox/interactions.gd): per item, rows in the item's own space. kind: the action id `used` names once the clip has run to its end (the rules hook). box: [x0,y0,z0,x1,y1,z1] what E aims at, or `on`: a prop's own box; stand: [x, z, yaw_deg] where the hero glides to, facing the stand's -Z, or without it where the clip's `grip` point (clips.json, default hand) meets the box, facing `face` (yaw_deg) or the way the hero comes. clip (data/clips.json), sound (audio.gd SOUNDS, played at the start), prompt. props: parts or made props (interactions.gd _prop); steps: [fraction of the clip, verb, prop, args] with the verbs appear, take, turn, glow, puff; `needs`: a prop that must still be there; `hold_s`: E must stay down this many seconds on the spot before it is used (interactions.gd `hold`: the body needs and the careful jobs; a row without it is used on the press); a prop named again in a later row of the item is the same one ({} will do). Motion and sound only, no game state (hard rule 1). HAB 1's units are placed from forge/hab_interior.py _mount (galley 351, desk 34, valves 58, brush 113, donning 129 degrees); the shelter's from forge/shelter_interior.py. pick: a greenhouse harvest takes the nearest head grown enough to eat off its tray (world.pick(); the step `pick` shows its prop, the head, in the glove for the clip), the stump regrows over the rules' sols (world.regrow()), and a tray with none left hides the prompt (14 Nov playtest: an endless lettuce). wiper: {bar: [m along the row, m high], role}: the row's item has a wiper, a bar across its panel_ part parked at the post's end; E at the spot (a control post on the row's junction box, the prop `post`, its button in the accent role) steps the hero to `stand` for the press, then the bar crosses the row in tuning.json interact.wiper_s and parks at the other end (the next press sends it back), the dust gone behind it; `used` once when it gets there, and the row is offered only while it is dusty and its wiper parked (world/sky_clock.gd dusty())

hab1._why: the lower berth (unit(berths, 218, 2.0) in forge/hab_interior.py): the air over its mattress, 1.25 to 1.75 m out along 218 degrees; E opens the sleep picker (cine/cine.gd)

the power panel (15 Nov): a switchboard on the bare wall between the galley's end (wall angle 11 degrees) and the desk (23), at 17.5 degrees, over the radio's box (its top is y 1.88) so the two never tie; E opens the switches card (sandbox.gd, `used` panel). No hold, no sound of its own

shelter._why: an air point on the front wall left of the door (its inner face is z -1.76, x -1.77 to -0.66; the open leaf swings to the right side): a plate and a bottle, made here

greenhouse._why: an air point on the vestibule's west wall (x -0.90, z -4.2 to -2.36; the open door leaf lies along the east one): a plate and a bottle, made here

mercou._why: E aims at a box round the pebble and its flag, 1.2 m square (in the item's own tilted space, its floor the ground there), not at the pebble's own box (`on`): 4 cm across, it was offered only while the hero walked straight at it and lost once they stood beside the flag (15 Nov playtest: 'no way to pick the pebble'). The first pebble's flag stands on the landmark `mercou`, the waypoint of s9_sample; the flags are 1.5 m with the pennant side on to the rover's stop, to be seen from it
